SPY 0DTE Defined-Risk Spread

Short 1% OTM put + long put W lower · held to expiry

✕REJECTED
Sharpe (real fills)0.30best cell 1% / $10 wide
Result+$1,113 vs +$4,073 nakedSame window as naked version
Max drawdown−17.2%— trades
Random baseline—2022 stress −$443 (Sh −0.39)

Tested at QG2's suggestion and rejected. The long put eats credit every day and almost never pays; with no early exit, a moderate down day costs the full strike width. It caps the tail but massively widens the body of the loss distribution. Correct answer is to keep the buy-to-close stop and add a cheap deep-OTM catastrophe put.

Source: s4_spread_findings.md

SPXW Triple Calendar (retest)

Same locked config, cash-settled index legs

✕FAIL
Sharpe (real fills)−0.381.39 at mid fill
Result−$3,753 at quarter fill2023 – 2026 (780 days)
Max drawdown−16% (mid) / sizing artifact otherwise— trades
Random baseline43%2022 stress n/a

Failed all three stress tests - worse than SPY. A real gross edge exists at mid (Sharpe 1.39, beats the index) but six legs of SPX dollar spread consume it entirely. One unresolved question: combos fill as a single net order, which backtesting on screen quotes cannot model. Only paper fills can settle it.

What the whole body of work says

  1. One clean pass. SPX/SPXW 0DTE short puts is the only strategy that cleared all three gates with real strength, and it is the only options strategy without an assignment tail. If anything gets capital first, it is this — via XSP for retail size, which is untested here because XSP is not on R2.
  2. Most of the 0DTE return is the volatility risk premium, not timing alpha. Selling the same put on random days already yields Sharpe ~0.87 on SPY. The 10:00 rule and event filter lift that to 1.26 — a real but modest selection benefit. On SPX the lift is much larger (random 0.50 → 1.07), which is why SPX ranks 98th percentile and SPY only 90th.
  3. The delta-neutral triple calendar hypothesis is dead on both SPY and SPXW. A genuine gross edge exists at mid-price; six legs of spread consume it entirely. The one thing backtesting cannot settle is combo net-fill quality — that needs paper fills, not more simulation.
  4. Re-tuning is the trap, not the parameters. On SPY, IWM and SPX alike, per-fold stop re-optimisation performed worse than a fixed stop. Lock the stop in the plateau region (3.5x SPY/IWM, 4.0–5.0x SPX) and leave it alone.
  5. Every 0DTE number here assumes the stop fills. The 2021–2026 window contains no flash crash, no limit-down day, no overnight gap through the strike. The historical worst day of −$547 is a statement about this window, not about the strategy's tail. A deep-OTM catastrophe put and/or cash-settled index options are the mitigation — the held-to-expiry spread was tested and is worse.
  6. GLD is a risk story, not a return story. It never beats buy-and-hold on return in any regime. It earns its PASS by halving the drawdown with a genuine, cost-surviving timing edge.
